rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿInd and ladā basically denote nearness, which may be literal or figurative according to context.
rows.anchor: وإذا ثبت إن عند ولدى للقرب فتارة يكون حقيقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿInd may mean before or behind when context supplies the sense of before; waraʾ may likewise mean before or near, depending on relational context.
rows.anchor: وقد تجىء بمعنى وراء وأمام إذا تضمنت معنى قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Between God and the Messenger’s hands implies deference and not advancing one’s own judgment or speech ahead of their command.
rows.anchor: وقد يطلق لتضمنه معنى الطواعية وترك الاختيار مع المخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿInd and ladā can denote literal nearness, as in the Prophet’s sighting at the Lote Tree and Joseph’s master at the door.
rows.anchor: فتارة يكون حقيقيا كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nearness to God can be figurative nearness of rank and favor; the angels described as near their Lord are the proximate angels.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا قيل الملائكة المقربون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿInd may express honor rather than physical location; the Prophet’s phrase alludes to the sphere of his community, since he is protected from error.
rows.anchor: كل ذلك عندي أي في دائرتي إشارة لأحوال أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the agreement about ten years, min ʿindik means by your favor and generosity.
rows.anchor: فإن أتممت عشرا فمن عندك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿInd can mean according to God’s judgment, as in describing liars, something grave, or a claim that something is true by God’s ruling.
rows.anchor: فأولئك عند الله هم الكاذبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In concise expressions such as from your Lord or a messenger from God, ʿind may be omitted while understood; the phrase from God makes the ellipsis clear.
rows.anchor: أي من عند الرحمن لظهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿInd can also mean presence, as when the throne was seen settled in the speaker’s presence.
rows.anchor: وقد تكون عند للحضور نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two commands about not preceding God and His Messenger and not raising voices combine the ranks of prophethood and messengership, recalling blessings in both.
rows.anchor: فكأنه جمع له المقامين معنى النبوة والرسالة تعديدا للنعم في الحالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an calls them the Prophet’s wives rather than the Messenger’s wives to mark their distinction from the rest of the community.
rows.anchor: لما قصد اختصاصهن عن بقية الامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title Prophet can introduce general legislation when a contextual clue broadens the address to the community, as in the plural divorce command.
rows.anchor: وقد يعبر بالنبي في مقام التشريع العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reproachful address forms يا أيها الذين كفروا and قل يا أيها الكافرون occur only in these two Qur’anic places because the form itself humiliates.
rows.anchor: ولتضمنه الإهانة لم يقع في القرآن في غير هذين الموضعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers are often mentioned in the third person as an expression of turning away from them, while believers are directly addressed with the order to fight.
rows.anchor: وكثر الخطاب ب يأيها الذين آمنوا على المواجهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Prophet reproached people, he used a courteous indirect formula such as asking what is wrong with men who do something.
rows.anchor: ولهذا كان صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا عتب على قوم قال ما بال رجال يفعلون كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing Adam to dwell in the Garden and the blessed greeting at its entry are examples of an address of honor.
rows.anchor: ويا آدم اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commands and declarations addressed to Iblis, including the threat of curse, are examples of humiliating address.
rows.anchor: فإنك رجيم وإن عليك اللعنة

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: The order to muster cavalry and infantry is not permission for Iblis to harm God’s servants; his efforts cannot gain authority over them.
rows.anchor: قالوا ليس هذا إباحة لإبليس وإنما معناه أن ما يكون منك لايضر عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to Abu Jahl is taḥakkum, a taunting reversal of his boast that no one between Mecca’s mountains was more mighty or noble than he.
rows.anchor: وهو خطاب لآبي جهل لأنه قال ما بين جبليها يعني مكة أعز ولا اكرم مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder that earlier messengers were rejected consoles the Prophet and tells him not to grieve but to remain patient.
rows.anchor: وإن يكذبوك فقد كذبت رسل من قبلك

words: إِن يَعُودُوا۟ فَقَدْ مَضَتْ سُنَّتُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the rejecters return to opposition, what befell earlier peoples will befall them.
rows.anchor: وإن يعودوا فقد مضت سنة الأولين

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن السراج
rows.claim: Al-Sarraj says deleting a particle is not analogical because particles already abbreviate verbs and their agents; deletion is permissible only when context makes the intended link clear.
rows.anchor: أخبرنا أبو علي قال قال أبو بكر بن السراج حذف الحرف ليس يقاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deleting a conjunction can make coordinated clauses feel like one, as in the omitted waw before do not spare you harm, and in the cited faces and Tabuk passages.
rows.anchor: فمنه الواو تحذف لقصد البلاغة فإن في إثباتها ما يقتضى تغاير المتعاطفين

rows.speaker: الفارسي
rows.claim: Al-Farisi estimates an omitted and I said before I find nothing, coordinating the phrase with they came; he treats they turned away as the answer to when.
rows.anchor: وخرج عليه الفارسي قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن الشجري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shajari rejects that coordination: the phrase is attached to the relative clause, which has no syntactic position, so neither does its coordinate.
rows.anchor: ومنعه ابن الشجري في أماليه وعلى هذا فلا موضع له من الإعراب

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the phrase as a circumstantial clause from the pronoun in they came, with an omitted saying, making it syntactically positioned as a حال.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري هي حال من الكاف في أتوك

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli says relief from blame depends on inability to find a mount, not on crying; the seven named men occasioned the verse, and their tears are a special virtue while the rule applies generally.
rows.anchor: قال السهيلي في أماليه ليس معنى الآية كما قالوا لأن رفع الحرج عن القوم ليس مشروطا بالبكاء عند التولي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When sunnah means the retributive fate of earlier nations, as in the Anfal verse, its spelling reflects this concrete action sense, supported by the surrounding warning and fight command.
rows.anchor: ويدل عليها أنها من الانتقام قوله قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same retribution sense appears in Fatir and al-Muʾmin; the surrounding verses establish that sunnah here is punishment.
rows.anchor: ويدلك على أنها بمعنى الانتقام قوله تعالى قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When sunnah means God’s law or way, it is an abstract name and its tāʾ is written closed, as in al-Ahzab and al-Israʾ.
rows.anchor: أما إذا كانت السنة بمعنى الشريعة والطريقة فهي ملكوتية بمعنى الاسم تقبض تاؤها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ in the written form of baqiyyat Allah is extended because it denotes tangible profit remaining in people’s property.
rows.anchor: فرد مدت تاؤه لأنه بمعنى ما يبقى فى أموالهم من الربح المحسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ of fiṭrat Allah is extended because the verse describes an actual created disposition on which people are made, as confirmed by the newborn-on-fitra report.
rows.anchor: فرد وصفها بأنها فطر الناس عليها فهى فصل خطاب فى الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurrata ʿayn in the report about Moses is extended as a present concrete event; qurrata aʿyun is closed because it is an abstract, unseen name.
rows.anchor: فرد مدت تاؤه لأنه بمعنى الفعل إذ هو خبر عن موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ of maʿṣiyat al-rasul is extended in two places in al-Mujadilah because it means the act of disobeying the Messenger, which the verse forbids.
rows.anchor: مدت فى موضعين فى سورة المجادلة لأن معناها الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two occurrences of laʿnah in the mutual imprecation and liʿan passages are extended because they denote an enacted curse.
rows.anchor: ومنه اللعنة مدت فى موضعين فى آية المباهلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tāʾ in the Tree of Zaqqūm is extended when eating it is foregrounded as an action, but closed when the tree is described as a named object and trial.
rows.anchor: لأنها بمعنى الفعل اللازم وهو تزقمها بالأكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed most hopeful verse is the debt passage: God’s care reaches even the recording of small debts, suggesting hope from such great concern for people.
rows.anchor: الأول آية الدين ومأخذه أن الله تعالى أرشد عباده إلى مصالحهم الدنيوية

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
rows.claim: Another candidate is the command that people of means forgive and ask whether they wish God to forgive them, cited in connection with the Ifk report and Ibn al-Mubarak.
rows.anchor: ولا يأتل أولوا الفضل منكم والسعة

words: إِن يَنتَهُوا۟ يُغْفَرْ لَهُم مَّا قَدْ سَلَفَ
rows.speaker: الشبلي
rows.claim: Al-Shibli calls the promise to forgive prior sins upon conversion the most hopeful: if God admits disbelievers who profess unity and testimony, He will not expel those who enter and remain.
rows.anchor: قل للذين كفروا إن ينتهوا يغفر لهم ما قد سلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourth proposal is the statement that only the ungrateful are requited.
rows.anchor: الرابع قوله تعالى ﴿ وهل نجازي إلا الكفور

words: إِنَّا قَدْ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْنَآ أَنَّ ٱلْعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed hopeful verse says punishment is for whoever denies and turns away.
rows.anchor: إنا قد أوحي إلينا أن العذاب على من كذب وتولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another candidate says that misfortunes follow people’s deeds, while God pardons much.
rows.anchor: وما أصابكم من مصيبة فبما كسبت أيديكم ويعفو عن كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage also lists the statement that each person acts according to their own disposition.
rows.anchor: قل كل يعمل على شاكلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposal is God’s promise to give until the Prophet is content.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi named feeding a near orphan or a destitute person as the most hopeful verse, according to the report from Ibn Abd al-Hakam in al-Harawi’s biography.
rows.anchor: يتيما ذا مقربة أو مسكينا ذا متربة

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi also called most hopeful the report that on Judgment Day each Muslim is given a disbeliever and takes him to the Fire.
rows.anchor: وسألته عن أرجى حديث للمؤمن قال حديث إذا كان يوم القيامة يدفع إلى كل مسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: In al-Hakim’s report from Ibn al-Munkadir, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr names God’s call to those who have transgressed as the most hopeful verse.
rows.anchor: التقى ابن عباس وعبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص فقال ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas prefers Abraham’s request for reassurance: God accepted his affirmation despite the heart’s exposure to Satanic whispering; al-Hakim called the report’s chain sound.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس أى آية فى كتاب الله أرجى عندك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The section asks about Qur’anic phrases that coincide with metrical poetry, whether a full line, several lines, or a hemistich, while treating such coincidence as distinct from poetry.
rows.anchor: فإن قيل فقد وجد فى القرآن ما وافق شعرا موزونا إما بيت تام أو أبيات أو مصراع

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They say the phrase about basins like reservoirs and firmly set cauldrons scans in ramal.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وجفان كالجواب وقدور راسيات ﴾ قالوا هذا من الرمل

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They say the purification phrase scans as a truncated khafif meter.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومن تزكى فإنما يتزكى لنفسه ﴾ قالوا هو مجزوء من الخفيف

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They say the promise of an exit and provision scans as mutaqārib if the word an exit is omitted from the measure.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومن يتق الله يجعل له مخرجا ويرزقه من حيث لا يحتسب ﴾ قالوا هو من المتقارب

rows.speaker: أبو نواس
rows.claim: They scan the shaded-gardens phrase as rajaz by lengthening the mīm; Abu Nuwas is said to have incorporated it into a poem.
rows.anchor: ويشبعون حركة الميم فيبقى من الرجز وحكى أن أبا نواس ضمنه فقال

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They say the phrase about confounding the enemy and healing believers’ hearts scans in wāfir.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويخزهم وينصركم عليهم ويشف صدور قوم مؤمنين ﴾ قالوا هو من الوافر

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They say the opening of al-Maʿun scans in khafif.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم ﴾ قالوا هو من الخفيف

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: They classify the opening oath sequences of al-ʿAdiyat and al-Dhariyat as basit meter.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والعاديات ضبحا فالموريات قدحا ﴾ ونحوه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adds Qur’anic phrases as examples of metrical coincidence, including night worship, charity, disputing, the flood, Abu Lahab, victory, conversion, and Qarun.
rows.anchor: نصر من الله وفتح قريب

rows.speaker: أعرابي
rows.claim: A Bedouin hearing a reciter objected that the recitation had broken the line; he was told it is the Qur’an, not poetry.
rows.anchor: ويحكى أنه سمع أعرابي قارئا يقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional إن is the most common use, including the promise that if disbelievers desist they are forgiven.
rows.anchor: الأول الشرطية وهو الكثير نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The default conditional إن leaves the speaker uncertain that the condition will occur; Jesus’ statement is an exception in form because he is certain he did not say it.
rows.anchor: ثم الاصل في عدم جزم المتكلم بوقوع الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن can introduce an event whose occurrence is certain but whose timing is unknown, such as the Prophet’s death.
rows.anchor: وقد تدخل على المتيقن وجوده اذا ابهم زمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن also occurs with an impossible hypothetical, as in the conditional claim that the Merciful had a son.
rows.anchor: وقد تدخل على المستحيل نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن points toward the future and makes even a formally past verb future; Ibn al-Hajib explains past-form examples by treating the event as the cause for the ensuing report.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن الحاجب وهي عكس لو فإنها للماضي وإن دخلت على المضارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With لم the jussive is attributed to لم, but with لا as in unless You forgive me, the jussive is attributed to إن.
rows.anchor: إن دخلت إن على لم يكن الجزم لم لابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لم cannot be separated from its verb, whereas إن may be separated from its governed verb by the verb’s own object; لا does not govern the verb, so the work falls to إن.
rows.anchor: والفرق بينهما إن لم عامل يلزم معموله ولا يفرق بينهما بشئ

words: إِن كُلُّ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ إِلَّآ ءَاتِى ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ عَبْدًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second إن functions like ما and enters nominal clauses in an exceptive construction, as in 19:93 and the listed parallel statements.
rows.anchor: الثاني بمنزلة لا وتدخل على الجملة الاسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Normally a conditional result is warranted by the condition’s actual occurrence: visiting warrants generosity, and gratitude warrants a visit.
rows.anchor: الثانية اصل الشرط والجزاء ان يتوفق الثاني على الاول بمعنى ان الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apparent counterexamples say the disciples are God’s servants whether punished or forgiven, and that the wives’ hearts had already swerved before repentance.
rows.anchor: وقد اورد على هذا آيات كريمات ومنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are not the true apodoses: in the punishment clause the omitted result is God’s authority over those who are His servants, which explains His power.
rows.anchor: والجواب ان هذه في الحقيقة ليست اجوبة وإنما جاءت عن الاجوبة المحذوفة لكونها اسبابا لها

rows.speaker: صاحب المستوفى
rows.claim: The author of al-Mustawfa says a conditional construction requires only that assuming the condition entails the result; it does not require temporal or causal dependence in either direction.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب المستوفى اعلم ان المجازاة لا يجب فيها ان يكون الجزاء موقوفا على الشرط أبدا

rows.speaker: صاحب المستوفى
rows.claim: The condition may fail to cause its result, as with a cold bath and retained heat, or may be necessarily paired with it, as sunrise and daylight.
rows.anchor: سواء كان الجزاء قد يقع لامن جهة وقوع الشرط كقول الطبيب

rows.speaker: صاحب المستوفى
rows.claim: The condition itself may be impossible, as in the hypothetical that the Merciful has a son.
rows.anchor: وسواء كان الشرط ممكنا في نفسه كالامثلة السابقة أو مستحيلا

rows.speaker: صاحب المستوفى
rows.claim: Condition and result may be causally linked, linked in the reverse direction, or merely paired without either causing the other, as in the cited belief, good-fortune, and guidance examples.
rows.anchor: وسواء كان الشرط سببا في الجزاء ووصله اليه

words: إِن يَنتَهُوا۟ يُغْفَرْ لَهُم مَّا قَدْ سَلَفَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent conflict between the two forgiveness promises disappears because the verse about Noah’s people addresses a different group from the promise to this community.
rows.anchor: فإن الآية التى فيها من قوم نوح والأخرى لهذه الأمة

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: An objection says partial forgiveness weakens the incentive to believe and conflicts with Islam erasing earlier sins, supporting al-Akhfash’s view that min is extra.
rows.anchor: فكيف يحسن التبعيض فيها مع إن الإسلام يجب ما قبله فيصح قول الأخفش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer limits the forgiveness in Noah’s story to worldly sins whose consequences included drowning; forgiveness in the afterlife through faith is understood.
rows.anchor: أحدها إن المراد بغفران بعض الذنوب في الدنيا لأن إغراق قوم نوح عذاب لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer notes that conversion does not erase obligations for wrongs against other people, so some sins remain for a convert.
rows.anchor: والثاني إن الكافر إذا آمن فقد بقي عليه ذنوب وهي مظالم العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because your sins can include past and future acts, min restricts the promise to past sins and avoids implying that faith alone pardons future disobedience.
rows.anchor: فقيل من لتفيد إن المغفور الماضي وعدم إطماعهم في غفران المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min may instead mark the starting point, which suits the explicit phrase what has gone before; Sibawayh preserves its partitive force by positing an omitted object, some of your sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنها لابتداء الغاية وهو حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed reading takes the ellipsis as magnifying the forgiveness: it covers a matter so tremendous that revealing its full nature would make people deem it immense.
rows.anchor: وقيل بل الحذف للتفخيم والتقدير يغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ما لو كشف لكم عن كنهه لاستعظمتم ذلك

rows.speaker: الصفار
rows.claim: Al-Saffar keeps min partitive: since forgive takes two objects, al-Akhfash makes the stated sins the second and treats min as extra, while the author’s group supplies an omitted object represented by the phrase.
rows.anchor: وقال الصفار من للتبعيض على بابها وذلك ان غفر تتعدى لمفعولين أحدهما باللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the charity verse min is partitive because giving charity does not erase every sin.
rows.anchor: فللتبعيض لأن أخذ الصدقة لا يمحو كل السيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istihza is making an insult heard, while sukhriya may be inward; the prophets’ wording uses mockery rather than the literal insulting act, which is not their conduct.
rows.anchor: والجواب أن الاستهزاء هو إسماع الإساءة والسخرية قد تكون في النفس ولهذا يقولون سخرت منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated mockery wording avoids using istihza because that act is not proper to prophets, and the verse already repeats mockery three times.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يقل نستهزىء بكم لأن الاستهزاء ليس من فعل الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s istihza means recompense for their action, since Arabic names a requital by the name of the original deed, as in God’s response to their forgetting Him.
rows.anchor: فالعرب تسمى الجزاء على الفعل باسم الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat that overtook mockers came from God through the messengers, answering the mockery they voiced; each word in the verse therefore retains its proper sense.
rows.anchor: أي حاق بهم من الله الوعيد البالغ لهم على ألسنة الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qibla command omits naming the Kaʿba because those far away need only face its direction; addressing the Prophet honors him, while explicit generalization confirms the rule for everyone.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر الكعبة لأن البعيد يكفيه مراعاة الجهة فإن استقبال عينها حرج عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When agreement can follow either a word’s form or its meaning, the Qur’an normally starts with singular grammatical agreement and then shifts to plural agreement for the sense.
rows.anchor: قاعدة إذا اجتمع الحمل على اللفظ والمعنى بدىء باللفظ ثم بالمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With whoever believes, the pronoun first agrees with the singular form, then the plural participle agrees with its meaning.
rows.anchor: فعاد الضمير من يدخله مفردا على لفظ من ثم قال خالدين وهو حال من الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further examples use singular-form clauses followed by plural meaning, with when He gave them of His bounty, they were miserly cited as an exception.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من عاهد الله لئن آتانا من فضله

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash treats min in lower your gaze and they have every kind of fruit as extra, meaning all gazes and all fruits.
rows.anchor: ومما احتج به الأخفش أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says min is partitive for gazes: only deliberate looking is prohibited, while accidental glances cannot be avoided and looking may be allowed for a proposal or instruction.
rows.anchor: وهذا ضعيف أيضا بل هي في الأول للتبعيض لإن النظر قد يكون عن تعمد وغير تعمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no min before the command to guard private parts because guarding them is universally required and can be fully controlled, unlike the gaze.
rows.anchor: من غير إعادة من لأن حفظ الفروج واجب مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise means each person in Paradise receives enough of every kind of fruit plus more, not every fruit God created; the latter would imply a finite store.
rows.anchor: فإن الله وعد أهل الجنة أن يكون لهم فيها كل نوع من أجناس الثمار مقدار ما يحتاجون إليه وزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min in the report of messengers is partitive, since other messengers were not related to the Prophet in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وأما الثالثة فللتبعيض بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A subtle distinction: forgiveness promises to believers omit min, while addresses to unbelievers use it, so the groups are not given equal promises; the latter is conditional and concerns sins against God, not people’s rights.
rows.anchor: لطيفة إنها حيث وقعت في خطاب المؤمنين لم تذكر كقوله في سورة الصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min in the statement that male and female hypocrites are of one another means association and allegiance, not descent, since children of hypocrites may be believers and vice versa.
rows.anchor: اي يلابس بعضهم بعضا ويواليه وليس المعنى على النسل والولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes valued occasions of revelation and wrote dedicated works; Ali ibn al-Madini and especially al-Wahidi are named, and the subject is not merely history.
rows.anchor: وقد اعتنى بذلك المفسرون في كتبهم وأفردوا فيه تصانيف منهم علي بن المديني شيخ البخاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing an occasion can reveal the wisdom that prompted a legal ruling.
rows.anchor: منها وجه الحكمة الباعثة على تشريع الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those who hold that the ruling follows the specific cause, the occasion can restrict the ruling to that cause.
rows.anchor: ومنها تخصيص الحكم به عند من يرى أن العبرة بخصوص السبب

rows.speaker: أبو الفتح القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri calls knowledge of the occasion a strong path to understanding the Qur’an; Companions gained it from contextual clues surrounding events.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ أبو الفتح القشيري بيان سبب النزول طريق قوى فى فهم معانى الكتاب العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When general wording has evidence for restriction, the case that occasioned it cannot be excluded by interpretation or consensus; its inclusion is certain, and earlier occasions affect later general wording.
rows.anchor: فإن محل السبب لا يجوز إخراجه بالاجتهاد والإجماع كما حكاه القاضي أبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects excluding the original case: it would delay explanation beyond need or turn from the question asked; the occasion definitively affects its case and may also weaken or defeat implications beyond it.
rows.anchor: أحدهما أنه يلزم منه تأخير البيان عن وقت الحاجة ولا يجوز والثاني أن فيه عدولا عن محل السؤال

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi says the food verse answers pagans who reversed what was lawful and forbidden; its ironic wording rejects their prohibitions on carrion, blood, pork, and offerings to others, without declaring all else lawful.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعى ما معناه فى معنى
